text:
Connor O'Brien: Coordinating RBAC v2 enablement for Hosted this week. Plan is shadow mode -> canary enforcement. Want to lock: timing, feature flags, dashboards, and rollback. @Kaitlyn Nguyen can you sanity check the flag names + what flips what?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: yep. In Hosted we have:
- `rbac_v2_shadow_eval_enabled` (dual-eval, no blocking)
- `rbac_v2_enforce_enabled` (enforce v2 decision)
- `rbac_v2_enforce_canary_pct` (org sampling)
Also `rbac_v2_log_decisions` is on by default in staging, optional in prod if we need to reduce volume.

Ethan Park: +1. In control-plane the middleware always runs, but the flag gates whether deny actually returns 403. Shadow mode still emits `authz_shadow_deny=true` metric + logs.

Connor O'Brien: Great. Proposed schedule (all times PT):
1) Tue 10:00 - enable shadow eval in prod (100% traffic)
2) Wed 11:00 - start canary enforce at 1% orgs
3) Thu - ramp to 10% if clean
4) Fri - ramp to 50% (or hold) depending on shadow denies + support load

Amara Diallo: For gateway: we’re not enforcing at gateway yet for Hosted, right? Just passing auth context through and service-level check does the decision.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: correct. Gateway only annotates actor/org/project and forwards `x-rw-actor-id` + `x-rw-org-id` + `x-rw-session` etc. Enforcement is in services. We do have standardized error response now (403 with `reason_code`).

Chloe Martin: Console backend is in scope too. We have a separate toggle `console_rbac_v2_enforce_enabled` (wired to same underlying evaluator but different rollout). Please don’t flip console enforcement same day as control-plane without a heads up—UX gets noisy fast when people see 403s on settings pages.

Connor O'Brien: Ack. For this thread I’m focusing on Hosted control-plane API enforcement. Console can stay shadow-only this week unless we explicitly decide otherwise.

Kevin Osei: Reminder: audit log enrichment is live behind `audit_authz_context_enabled`. If we’re canary enforcing, we should at least have decision context for those denies (policy_version, role_ids, decision_reason) or we’ll get “why was I blocked” questions with no evidence.

Marcus Lin: +1. From security perspective, first week of enforcement must include:
- authz decision context in audit logs for denied ops
- monitoring/alerts for spikes in deny (real + shadow)
- a known-good rollback path (flag + revert policy bundle)

Sean Gallagher: SRE angle: need guardrails if enforcement causes an outage pattern (e.g., org-admin blocked from rotating keys). What’s the auto-abort threshold? We should predefine a rollback trigger.

Connor O'Brien: Proposed rollback triggers:
- p95 403 rate > 2% of control-plane requests for 10 min (excluding known forbidden endpoints)
- any P0 customer impact report in #help within first hour
- authz eval latency p95 > 5ms sustained (we saw 1-2ms in staging)
Rollback action: set `rbac_v2_enforce_canary_pct=0` then disable `rbac_v2_enforce_enabled`.

Leila Farouk: For monitoring, I can set up a quick dashboard panel set:
- `authz_eval_latency_ms` (p50/p95)
- `authz_policy_cache_hit_rate`
- `http_403_rate` with breakdown by `reason_code`
- `authz_shadow_deny_rate` by endpoint
Also a canary-only view by org cohort if we can tag it.

Ethan Park: We can tag canary orgs in logs (field `rbac_v2_canary=true`) and metrics label `cohort=canary` (already in the middleware from last PR). Should show up once canary is non-zero.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: One more gotcha: policy cache invalidation. If role assignment changes, we invalidate per-org, but if invalidation fails, enforcement can “lag” until TTL (5m). We added metrics `authz_policy_cache_invalidation_errors`. Please watch that.

Incident Bot: (auto) FYI: previous staging incident 2025-02-12 involved Billing Admin blocked from updating payment method due to missing `billing.*` allow in default role bundle. Resolved via policy bundle v0.1.3.

Connor O'Brien: thanks bot. Let’s explicitly verify policy bundle version. @Kaitlyn Nguyen what policy bundle is in prod right now?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: prod is currently pinned to `policy_bundle_version=0.1.3` (same as last week’s rollout). v0.1.4 is in rc with additional Dedicated perms; shouldn’t affect Hosted, but we can keep Hosted on 0.1.3 for this rollout to minimize variables.

Marcus Lin: Please keep policy stable for the enforcement flip. Change one thing at a time.

Amara Diallo: For customer-facing behavior: 403 error includes `reason_code=RBAC_V2_FORBIDDEN` + `required_permission`? (Some SDKs print this.) Want to ensure we don’t leak internal action names.

Ethan Park: Today it returns `required_permission` (like `org.keys.rotate`) and `resource_scope` (org/project). We decided that’s acceptable for developer UX; doesn’t expose secrets, just tells them what they need. Security ok’d it in design review.

Kevin Osei: On audit logs: make sure denies generate an audit event only for P0/P1 actions. We don’t want an event storm from read-only endpoints returning 403.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: agreed. Current behavior: authz decision context is attached to existing audit events for “audited actions” (key mgmt, billing changes, SSO config, org membership). Pure denies without an audited action don’t create a new event, but logs still contain decision fields.

Chloe Martin: Support heads up: once enforcement canary starts, we should alert #help with the reason_code + how to check shadow vs real deny. Otherwise we’ll get “random 403s” tickets.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll post a short note in #help + #eng-platform before Wed canary. Also adding to runbook: how to identify if org is in canary cohort.

Sean Gallagher: Who’s on point during the first hour of canary? Need a named person watching the dashboard + ready to flip pct to 0.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll be primary (10:45-12:00 Wed). Backup: @Kaitlyn Nguyen for policy/questions, @Ethan Park for service behavior. If I’m offline, SRE can flip the flag but please ping us.

Leila Farouk: I’ll prep the dashboard + an alert: `authz_shadow_deny_rate` > baseline + `http_403_rate{cohort=canary}` spikes. Will drop link here when ready.

Redwood Deploy Bot: (auto) Change request created: "Enable RBAC v2 shadow evaluation in prod" scheduled for 2025-02-18 10:00 PT. Approvers: Connor O'Brien, Marcus Lin.

Marcus Lin: approved for shadow mode. For enforcement canary, require explicit go/no-go in this thread after 24h of shadow data.

Connor O'Brien: works. Action items:
- Leila: dashboard + alerts
- Kevin: confirm audit export pipeline handling new authz fields (no schema breaks)
- Kaitlyn/Ethan: confirm prod flags + policy pinned 0.1.3
- Connor: comms to #help and runbook snippet
We’ll reconvene Wed 10:30 PT for go/no-go based on shadow denies.

Kevin Osei: Exporter is backward-compatible; new fields are optional. I’ll still run a dry-run check on SIEM mapping today.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: I’ll paste the exact flag values and the launch commands in a reply before Tue.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup:
